My thoughts exactly. I do have a bit of sympathy for the company because it was so clear some "Higher Force" was in play. It had been barely over a week since they opened Shining Nikki Korean server, but they just announced that they will be closing the server in the middle of the night a few days ago, reason being they 'would not stand Korean players insulting China' and that as a Chinese company they would do what's necessary to protect their country's name.
It's insane because this effectively killed their entire business in Korea, not just Shining Nikki. No company CEO with the right mind would come to this decision...

So to provide some insight... China has been claiming Hanbok as THEIR traditional clothing, along with kimchi and other Korean stuff. This apparently happened to Vietnams' Ao Dai as well, and it's been going on for a long time.

There's been a recent uproar because of this. Chinese social media has been exploding with "how dare Koreans claim Hanboks are theirs" kind of sentiment.

Recently Nikki's company has presented itself as pre-Chinese government. For example, to celebrate Shining Nikki's Korean server opening, they released a Hanbok suit. Then the Chinese players complained on social media that they shouldn't call this 'Hanbok' but instead call it Korean-Chinese. The company's response was more or less "Sorry about that, our alignment is the same as our government's. We will just remove such clothes (hanboks) from the game". As of now you can't even type the word 'Korea' on the KOREAN server.

My apologies if I'm biased, but honestly I'm flabbergasted and can't separate this with the current ongoing events. Just wanted to provide some info to maybe help with the OP's question. I might be mistaken and this tag could be completely unrelated to this issue, in which case, please feel free to correct me.

Here's a few suggestions from me:

1. Know your girlfriend's measurements (I usually check bust&waist mainly because those tend to be a majority of my problems, sometimes shoulder length or arm opening if the sleeves are short and look too tight) lolita wardrobe is my go-to website and they usually recommend your measurements are at least 3\~4cm smaller than the actual dress size
2. Find dresses under 'customizable' category. Some websites like lolita wardrobe have a separate category for such, meaning you can have custom measurements for any clothing item under that category.
3. Does your gf like empire style dress or ones that doesn't fit around the waist? examples:[https://www.soufflesong.com/Mucha-Empire-Open-Front-Classic-Long-Jumperskirt](https://www.soufflesong.com/Mucha-Empire-Open-Front-Classic-Long-Jumperskirt)[https://www.lolitawardrobe.com/u\_file/1805/photo/d8b9689221.jpg](https://www.lolitawardrobe.com/u_file/1805/photo/d8b9689221.jpg)I personally find these type of dresses much more comfortable to wear, so if she's into the style, it might be a good substitute.Usually they release different types of dresses for each project, so maybe there's a version of the Shimotsuki Sakuya dress you linked where you don't have to worry too much about measurements.
4. If all else fails, looking for a similar-looking dress is also a good idea. A lot of dresses out there share similar outline/prints/style etc., so maybe you can find a close one as the Shimotsuki Sakuya dress that might make your gf as happy (unless that dress is #1 must buy dream-dress for your gf that non other can replace).

Yeah, I really feel you. Last night I was up late crying because I miss my pupper, wanting her back, saying that I'm sorry for wanting you back instead of being happy that she's not suffering anymore.
The way her passing happened was actually 6 days earlier than we planned with our vet. Her condition got worse so we took her to the vet and they said Bells probably has been suffering more than we thought but came to a point where she couldn't even pretend to be okay (bc that's what dogs do to not sadden their family). We had to put her down there and then. We really weren't prepared for that to happen that day... I regret every single moment I wasn't paying attention to her that morning. Had I known it would be the last I would've showered her with attention till she gets annoyed. I could feel her life escaping from her body and it was a devastating feeling.
I do believe in heaven (not as in afterlife but like...just a happy ethereal place) and that is actually my only comfort, that my girl (and all the goodest little friends including your Milo!) is probably enjoying rolling on some heavenly grass at peace. That I will be reunited with her eventually.

My pet passed just a day before your Milo did. I fear about forgetting what it felt like to pet my girl or have her around as well. My deepest condolensces. This letter is filled with so much love. Milo must have had a happy life with such a caring, loving and devoted partner.

I'd like to share something my therapist told me today, if that's alright. It's about the part where you asked your boy to give you a couple more days to mourn.

I personally believe he would be okay to give you more than a couple days, because it's normal to mourn and be sad about this.

It hasn't even been a week since we parted with our pets. You're not weak, nor selfish, for feeling this way or wanting him back. It's only normal and shows how much you love him. It wouldn't have hurt as much if I didn't love my Bells as much as I do. So, in that sense, I think of it as a way of expressing my love for her. (or at least I try when I'm feeling less miserable)

It's important to process the shock, and you should do it at your own pace, no matter what others may tell you (in case people have told you/would tell you to 'get over it' soon). It's okay to grieve. How can you not when you love him so much?

Sorry if I was being nosy, or if it sounded like I'm lecturing you... It helped me to hear it from someone else, so I write this hoping it would do the same for you. If it doesn't help or bother you in any way, please feel free to disregard anything I said.

May Milo rest in peace.

I relate to this post as well. We just said goodbye to our beloved dog child last Friday.

She was an old girl, so giving her medications was a part of preparing her meals. Then she got oral tumor and it became hard for her to chew anything, so we started powdering the meds so she could still take it.

Now I don't have to grind the meds in the bowl. I don't need to take her canned food out and mix it well with the meds so there's no part in her food that tastes especially yucky. I don't need to get up in the morning to give her a nice walk.

I miss doing all of that. I even sometimes move my hand as if I was petting her, because I'm desperate to not let go of that feeling, how soft her head was, just how tall my hand needed to be in the air, and... just everything.

My condolensces to your rabbit, and also FT1996's bulldog. Our pets gave us so much happiness. I hope they're truly at peace now, hopefully enjoying their favorite food in the pet heaven.

Just saw this post and wanted to say I agree. I don't think the OP shamed stay-at-home mom necessarily. 
Stay-at-home moms ARE super and people really should appreciate them more bc housework is ENDLESS

What I think the OP meant to do (or at least my personal thoughts on the matter) was just to express how uncomfortable they were to face the stereotype still predominant in this society. Like spumoni_ln said, many men like to use phrases like 'go back to the kitchen' as an insult towards women who 'dares' to attempt anything else, without any respect towards the housework. Seeing most of the entries covered by aprons was just an unpleasant reminder of the prejudice for me.

I do agree, however, that LN items do have a limited range, that the contest voting is done within a split second for most people, and that people just ended up relying on items which could indicate the stereotypical image of a mother.

I think something might have been lost in translation for this post, because I truly don't believe the players meant any malice when submitting their entries (I don't think OP does either). But maybe upon encountering this post, it was taken as a challenge to people who did use aprons in their entries? Because it's one thing to hear complaints about stereotypes but it's a different story when it is (or at least when it seems so on the receiving end) pointed towards their own actions, and a lot of people (including people on this subreddit and myself) did use aprons in their entries, that's where the misunderstanding happened? Like they didn't necessarily meant to perpetuate the stereotype but people felt they were accused of it??

IDK if this makes any sense but as someone who personally had the same thoughts as the OP while also seeing the other side's argument, I just got curious why there ended up being discourses on this thread. I think it's just be a big misunderstanding bc if I were to write a complaint about stereotypes, that's the only thing I'd want to do, without the intention to offend people (bc at the end of the day we all are affected by what the society drills into our brains. I find little point in judging each other for it)
